post.description: Validates email and password credentials. When MFA is enabled on the account a one-time code is sent via email and the response contains a short-lived ``temp_token`` instead of a full access token. Submit that ``temp_token`` together with the received code to ``POST /auth/mfa/verify`` to obtain a full JWT. After repeated failures the account is progressively locked following a J-curve schedule; the lock duration doubles with every additional failed attempt beyond the stage-2 threshold.
Sends a one-time password reset link to the registered email address. The response is always identical regardless of whether the email is registered, to prevent user enumeration.
Verify if an invite token is valid without consuming it.
Verify if a reset password token is valid without consuming it.

post.summary: Reset password using a one-time token
post.description: Validates the one-time token from the reset or invitation email and sets a new password.  Invited accounts (``invitation_status='Pending'``) are automatically transitioned to ``'Accepted'`` on success.  Tokens expire after 24 hours and are single-use.
Generates a new MFA code if the previous 2-minute window has expired.

Validates the emailed OTP against the ``temp_token`` issued during the ``/login`` step. Returns a full JWT access token on success. The temp token expires after 2 minutes. Repeated failures trigger progressive MFA lockouts on the same J-curve schedule as login failures.

Revokes the bearer access token by persisting its ``jti`` claim in the ``revoked_tokens`` table.  Subsequent requests using the same token are rejected with HTTP 401 even if the token has not yet expired. The client should discard the token after calling this endpoint.

Updates the password for the currently authenticated user. On success the current access token is immediately revoked so the user must log in again — matching the user story requirement that the session is terminated after a password change.

post.summary: Create organization and trigger tenant DB provisioning

Handles both the forgot-password flow and first-time password setting
for newly invited Tenant Users.  On success:

* The user's ``hashed_password`` is updated.

        ``confirm_password``, and ``org_id``.
    master_session: Injected async database session (master DB).

Returns:
    A success dict with a confirmation message.

Raises:
    HTTPException 400: Token is invalid, expired, or already consumed.

post.summary: Get validation status for pending claims in a batch
post.description:
Retrieves the validation status, progress, and metadata for a batch of claims,
returning only the claims that are still pending AI processing.

**Request Body:**
- `claim_ids`: list of UUID or string identifiers of the claims to check

**Response:**
- A list of claim status entries, one per claim currently in `Pending` ai_status.
  Claims that were not found, or are no longer pending, are simply omitted.

**Response Fields (per item):**
- `ai_status`: Current validation state (always PENDING for items in this response)
- `ai_processing_progress`: Progress percentage (0-100)
- `ai_processing_stage`: Current processing stage (e.g., "Documents Parsing", "Rule Validation")
- `compliance_score`: Final compliance score (when complete)

**Frontend Usage:**
```javascript
// Poll this endpoint every 1-2 seconds during processing
const response = await fetch('/api/v1/organization/claims/status', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
    body: JSON.stringify({claim_ids: ['claim-uuid-1', 'claim-uuid-2']})
});
const data = await response.json();
// data only contains the claims that are still pending
data.forEach(item => console.log(`${item.claim_id}: ${item.ai_processing_progress}% - ${item.ai_processing_stage}`));
```

Block minutes must be positive.  Multiplier must be ≥ 1.0.

app__schemas__dashboard__DashboardMetric.title: DashboardMetricsRequest
app__schemas__dashboard__DashboardMetric.description:
Single request payload for the combined dashboard metrics endpoint.

Date filter (applied globally to all 8 KPI counters):
* Supply ``range`` (0 = today, 7/15/30/60/90 = last N days)  **or**
* Supply both ``custom_from`` + ``custom_to`` for a custom date window.
When both are present, the custom range takes precedence.

Year filter (applied to graph series only):
* Supply ``year`` to display upload and compliance trends for a specific calendar year.
* Defaults to the current year if not specified.
* Graph data shows all 12 months (Jan-Dec) for the selected year,
  regardless of the KPI date filter.
